Forty-four years ago, after completing a degree in Fine Art from the University of Guelph in Ontario, Laking moved to Nova Scotia with the expectation of being here a year or two and then moving west. The ocean, the people, the old villages, the pace of life, and the natural beauty captured her heart and now she is undoubtedly one of our province’s favourite artists.

I love Nova Scotia, said Laking. For many years, I felt most at home with the rocks and water of the wild Atlantic. Gradually the beauty of the Bay of Fundy, with its huge tides and vast mud flats wormed its way into my soul. Now I am like an old tree that has put down its roots and I am truly happy. We live in the middle of blueberry country; Jim and I actually have a blueberry patch on our property, so for many, many years I have painted blueberry blossoms, and blueberries. The past two years, I have done at least one large oil each year of the berries. I sit in a blueberry field for a number of days and paint en plein air.

This past week, I was sitting outside for my second day of work on a painting for Out of the Blue when the wind made painting on location almost impossible. On a really windy day, I can only paint a small watercolour on location because I can anchor it with my body. My large oil on a wobbly easel was continually swaying and I was forced to move across the road where I was sheltered by trees.

I was able to continue, but I couldnt clearly see this years subject of blueberries. This year, I am trying to capture blueberries as they ripen. The July blueberry flowers are gone and now there are tiny green berries that are turning to pink and then to blue. Then the blueberries gradually increase in size until they are all sweet, plump, delicious and ready to harvest.

Laking usually paints within an hour of her home in Portaupique, between Great Village and Bass River. She also believes it is important every year to paint in unfamiliar places so she can return home with fresh eyes. This year she painted in Africa for two months and then a couple of weeks ago, she had the privilege of being this years Port Bickerton Lighthouse Resident Artist. She spent 14 days capturing the beauty of this special area including the fog, and the tides on Nova Scotias eastern shore.

In addition to painting in unfamiliar surroundings, I also reinvigorate my creative life, by trying unfamiliar mediums, as well as unfamiliar materials, new papers and new approaches, said Laking.

Out of the Blue, leaves an artist a wide range of freedom for creative expression, so it will be interesting to see what each artist brings to the show. We will be hanging the show on Sunday and the opening reception will be held Monday, Aug. 29 at 6:30 p.m. We invite everyone to join us in celebrating our province’s bountiful beauty and would love to hear feedback from you. The show runs to Sept. 2.

About Art: The world through Joy Laking's eyes
----------------------------------------------

Joy Laking loves to paint.

By Staff, PNI Atlantic 

Last updated Sep 30, 2017

![Image 1: Local resident Joy Laking is excited to offer her annual fall open house exhibition. Dozens of pieces of artwork will be featured in the open house in which Laking showcases the beauty of Nova Scotia.](https://smartcdn.gprod.postmedia.digital/saltwire/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/joy-laking-2964030_medium.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=288&h=216&sig=SB-ayT6TQqsGo3UrKmiEWw)

Local resident Joy Laking is excited to offer her annual fall open house exhibition. Dozens of pieces of artwork will be featured in the open house in which Laking showcases the beauty of Nova Scotia.

For 41 years she has painted Nova Scotia and captured her view of the world with watercolour, oil and acrylics. She is inspired by all of the beauty that is Nova Scotia and whenever possible Laking paints on location. She has exhibited provincially, nationally and internationally and she is the recipient of numerous awards.

For 25 years every October she has held an open house and many people look forward to it.

**Q. Why do you have an open house every year?**

A. The yearly open house exhibition gives me a chance to just focus on all of the new paintings for the year and it certainly keeps me motivated to make sure I have 40 new works that I am very proud of. It is the one time of the year when everything is hung just the way I want it to be. The rest of the year, works are sold and new works are put up in their place with no thought about groupings or themes. It is also a time when I am sure to be home and not painting. Folks aren’t interrupting me. They are doing me a favour to stop in.

**Q. Why do you enjoy the open house?**

A. Before the open house, I worry that I won’t be able to produce another exhibition that is new and visually exciting. Somehow through faith and hard work, everything comes together and I have a show that I am proud of. Then I just get to enjoy looking at a current year’s paintings and I can relax and visit with all the friends that come to see this show.

**Q. What provided inspiration for this year’s show?**

A. This summer I spent at least a week painting in Port Hawkesbury, Advocate, Tatamagouche and Parrsboro and the scenery in Bass River and Great Village is always a constant inspiration for me. Six paintings and 15 sketches are from my England trip which are very special because they are of the English towns where my maternal grandparents grew up. Several of my other paintings feature snow and the glorious winter that we experienced. With watercolours, I don’t use any white paint, and so it is like magic to create snow with just a little hint of shadows or by using roads and buildings to delineate the snow.

In 1982, I had my first solo exhibition at the Mount Saint Vincent University Art Gallery. The entire exhibition was of white flowers on white paper done in watercolour. Thirty-three years later, I am still excited about this challenge of white-on- white. In addition to all the new paintings, there are four new prints and a new selection of greeting cards.

**Q. Who would you like to attend your open house?**

A. I would love to have everyone come, the old, the young, the buyers, the lookers. I would especially love to have folks who might never have been in an art gallery come to the open house. By looking at the paintings, they will enjoy the beauty of Nova Scotia and the world through my eyes and then we can have a cup of tea together and I can answer any questions they might have.

**Q. When is it?**

A. My 2015 open house exhibition is Oct. 17, 18, 24 and 25, from 10 a.m. until 5 p.m. at the Joy Laking Gallery, 6730 Hwy #2, Bass River. The paintings can also be viewed on line at www.joylakinggallery.com.
